text: oh, i guess this is relevant also, but if you look at the water painting tool. im pretty sure if i remember correctly, it requres that you have to have a negative heightfield to then be able to paint in water. but as it stands, the heightfield tool is only allowed to do positive. now, i kinda also think this is kinda a bad hack if you ask me, and that the water tool should do its own negative depth on any terrain, that way you know for example you could put a river flowing down a hill. also, we are working inside of the @cart/editor/ and not hmsc-int so dont be confused :) i see you searching in the one location so just to keep it on track
resolution: Water brush now carves its own bed instead of only filling pre-dug sub-zero basins: each covered sample digs depth×brushweight below the pre-stroke surface and fills exactly the carved volume, so the water surface sits at the original grade and FOLLOWS terrain — a river painted down a hill flows downhill. Wet samples reconstruct their pre-stroke surface as bed+depth, making re-drags idempotent (no runaway trenching); erase still drains without re-filling the carve. Water channel gained a DEPTH stepper (1-64m) in the map paint bar; engine test rewritten and all 39 pass. Needs a dev-host rebuild.
